profile.name: Mawuli Badassou
profile.title: DevOps & Data Engineer | AWS Certified Solutions Architect
profile.bio: DevOps and data engineer with 2+ years of experience spanning cloud infrastructure and production data pipelines. Automates AWS infrastructure with IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation), CI/CD and observability, and builds and tunes Spark pipelines for a financial services data platform. Background in backend development supports direct collaboration across engineering teams.

experience.description: Designing and automating multi-environment AWS infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and production observability, and building and tuning Spark ETL pipelines for a financial services data product.
responsibilities: Built core extractors and business logic for the Spark ETL pipeline behind a financial services data product; took the management fees engine end to end, validated against the legacy system on over 99% of checks
Halved pipeline runtime, 218 to ~105 minutes, by profiling where time was spent, narrowing a shared dataset from 377 to ~147 columns, and consolidating 103 extractors to ~40
Diagnosed defects that were silently dropping data, including a shared-attribute collision that made extractors read the wrong source columns; added guard tests blocking the whole bug class
Deputized for the data team lead during absences and reviewed team pull requests, flagging issues before merge

Restructured and fully imported a multi-environment (dev/staging/prod) AWS infrastructure into Terraform; built a reusable modules library to standardize and accelerate infrastructure provisioning across all cloud accounts

Set up Prometheus and Grafana for production monitoring; diagnosed a critical outage by tracing a memory leak through metrics and logs, coordinated the fix with the backend team, and added service-level CPU/memory limits and alerting to prevent recurrence

Built custom Grafana dashboards tracking API Gateway metrics — request rate, response time, response size, and rate-limit violations — with threshold-based alerting to surface performance issues early
Deployed Jaeger for distributed tracing, providing end-to-end visibility into request flows across services and making latency bottlenecks and failure points traceable

Designed and validated a disaster recovery strategy: configured deletion protection, DynamoDB backups, and AWS Backup; ran a full DR simulation achieving RTO of 16 min (target: 20 min) with RPO of 24 hours
Cleared a storage crisis on production instances — from 90–93% down to 53–55% — by purging stale deployment artifacts and tightening revision retention, preventing future deployment failures
Introduced Ansible for post-provisioning configuration, automating Nginx/SSL setup, package installs, and environment variable management across environments and eliminating manual SSH access
Integrated database migration execution into the CI/CD build phase, ensuring schema changes are applied before application startup and preventing environment drift
Migrated the production email system to AWS SES and refactored the sending layer with connection pooling and parallel processing, improving throughput and removing reliability bottlenecks
Automated dev/staging environment shutdowns outside business hours, cutting compute costs by ~45–50%
achievements: Halved Spark pipeline runtime from 218 to ~105 minutes with zero data loss
Management fees engine matched 3,811 of 3,843 legacy anchor values exactly
Won the DevOps Week hackathon as part of a team
Achieved RTO of 16 min (vs. 20 min target) in full DR simulation with 24h RPO
Migrated 12+ manually created AWS resources into reusable Terraform modules across dev/staging/prod
Cut compute costs by ~45–50% through scheduled non-production shutdowns
Cleared production storage from 90–93% to 53–55% utilization, preventing deployment failures
Diagnosed and resolved a critical production memory leak through Prometheus/Grafana observability

projects.title: Dynamiq Concept
projects.description: Full-stack platform for a Ghanaian photography studio: portfolio, session booking with deposits, and a data/airtime shop, all on one Next.js deployment.
projects.longDescription: Built and run end to end for a photography and videography business in Ghana. Two businesses share one Next.js deployment: the dark-themed photography site handles portfolio, services, and a multi-step booking flow (pay in full, pay a deposit, or pay after the shoot), while a separate light-themed shop sells data and airtime through a cart and checkout. A single admin panel manages bookings, orders, products, services, gallery, testimonials, blocked dates, and site settings. Payments run through two scoped Paystack merchant accounts behind one webhook that verifies against both keys, records every event for idempotency, and derives booking status from the running total of successful payments, including manually recorded cash and Mobile Money payments.
highlights: 🌐 Live in production: booking, payments, and shop
Booking flow with full, deposit, and pay-after-work options plus an availability calendar
Two Paystack merchant accounts behind one idempotent, signature-verified webhook
Admin panel for bookings, orders, catalog, gallery, and offline payment recording
Per-IP rate limiting, hashed reset tokens, JSON-LD, sitemap, and IndexNow for SEO

projects.title: Multi-Region DR Automation (Terraform)
projects.description: Pilot-light disaster recovery across two AWS regions: a Route 53 health check triggers a Lambda that scales up the standby fleet and promotes the RDS replica, with no manual steps.
projects.longDescription: Solo capstone for my DevOps training. The whole stack is defined in Terraform across 13 reusable modules spanning three regions. The primary region runs an ALB, Auto Scaling group, and RDS MySQL, while the secondary region idles at zero instances with an encrypted cross-region read replica and S3 cross-region replication. A Route 53 health check flips DNS to the secondary ALB, and a CloudWatch alarm in us-east-1 invokes a Python Lambda that scales the standby fleet up, promotes the replica, and reports progress over SNS. The repo documents the architecture, a failover demo, and the known limitations.
highlights: 🎓 Solo capstone: DevOps training
Automated failover: health check → CloudWatch alarm → Lambda
Standby fleet scaled from 0 and RDS read replica promoted on failover
S3 cross-region replication and KMS-encrypted replica
13 Terraform modules across three regions, validated in CI
